answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to deter Sybil attacks. Agents invest in an opal deposit, which is forfeited upon detection of identity duplication. The timber of punishment is amplified through a grove of correlated equilibria, wherein expected payoffs from honest participation strictly dominate those of Sybilized strategies, rendering identity multiplication unprofitable and guaranteeing a strict Nash equilibrium.
